title: PromptPack terms
description: Generic terms minted by RFC 0016 for slots the Data Privacy Vocabulary does not address because they are not about personal data. No external instrument defines these terms; PromptPack does, and their definitions do not change. A term that needed to change would be deprecated and replaced, never redefined.

terms.label: Confidential
terms.definition: Information whose disclosure outside its authorised audience would harm the organisation or the people it concerns. Organisations map their own classification schemes onto this term.

terms.label: Restricted
terms.definition: Information whose disclosure would cause serious harm, with access limited to named roles. Stricter than Confidential.

terms.label: Public
terms.definition: Information approved for disclosure without restriction.

terms.label: Credentials
terms.definition: Secrets that authenticate a person, service or system: passwords, API keys, access tokens and private keys.

terms.label: Financial account
terms.definition: Identifiers and details of a financial account, such as account and card numbers, balances and transactions.

terms.label: Synthetic media
terms.definition: Generating or manipulating image, audio, video or text content that resembles real people, objects, places or events and could falsely appear authentic.

terms.label: Bias testing
terms.definition: Testing whether the agent's outputs or the outcomes they lead to differ without justification across groups of people.

terms.label: Accuracy review
terms.definition: Reviewing whether the agent's outputs meet the accuracy declared for its intended purpose.

terms.label: Red teaming
terms.definition: Adversarial testing in which testers try to make the agent act outside its intended purpose or declared limits.

terms.label: Data quality review
terms.definition: Reviewing whether the data the agent uses or produces is fit for its intended purpose: complete, accurate, relevant and, where required, de-identified.

terms.label: Human oversight review
terms.definition: Reviewing whether human oversight of the agent works as declared: that the people overseeing it can understand its outputs, intervene, and override or stop it.
